item.title: Essential Bash Special Variables Explained: Positional Parameters and Shell State
item.description:
“Essential Bash Special Variables Explained: Positional Parameters and Shell State”

When developing robust shell scripts, access to specific contextual information provided by the shell itself is crucial. These are encapsulated in predefined, unique variables known as special parameters. Let’s delineate their specific roles and applications.

Positional Parameters and Argument Handling

Positional parameters directly correspond to the arguments supplied when invoking a script or function.

  • $1, $2, $3, …: These represent the individual positional arguments passed to the script or function. For instance, $1 is the first argument, $2 is the second, and so forth.
